title: Venezuela Trans-Andean Highway
slogan: Barinas to Merida · 136 km home again

waypoints.name: Barinas
waypoints.advice: Barinas is where the day begins. Next is Santo Domingo, 86 km on.

waypoints.name: Santo Domingo
waypoints.advice: Santo Domingo comes up 86 km in. Next is Pico El Aguila Pass, 85 km on.

waypoints.name: Pico El Aguila Pass
waypoints.advice: 171 km in you reach Pico El Aguila Pass. The road climbs 4118 m over the 85 km before it, hard. Reckon on about 27 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Nothing on this route is higher. Next is Merida, 86 km on and mostly downhill.

sections.advice: Barinas → Santo Domingo is 75 km of getting across. Ride it tidily and keep the enthusiasm for what comes after.
Santo Domingo → Pico El Aguila Pass climbs about 4118 m in 19 km. This is the part worth slowing down for - look through the bends and use the pull-offs.
Pico El Aguila Pass → Merida drops about 4118 m over 58 km. Brakes and eyes forward; the views are behind the corners, not in them.

provenance: CURATED FROM THE ARCHIVE: waypoints taken from the named road Venezuela Trans-Andean Highway. Distances between stops are great-circle with a road factor, not a routed measurement - the pipeline replaces them when it routes this line.

scenicChapters.title: Venezuela Trans-Andean Highway
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 4118 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance — cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Pico El Aguila Pass → Merida
scenicChapters.narrative: 4118 m come off over 98 km at around 7.1%. The road gives back what the climb took, faster than it took it. Brakes early, eyes far ahead. A descent this long asks more of concentration than of pace.
